title: Paired Battery Storage under Net Energy Metering Riders
content:
A battery may be paired with a Net Energy Metering system only under a rider that allows storage, and only up to that rider's storage capacity limit.

| Rider | Battery may be paired | Largest paired battery (kWh) | Grid-charged battery energy may be exported for credit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rider NEM-L Legacy Net Energy Metering | No | 0 | No |
| Rider NEM-R Residential Net Energy Metering | Yes | 40 | No |
| Rider NBT-R Residential Net Billing Tariff | Yes | 40 | No |
| Rider NBT-C Commercial Net Billing Tariff | Yes | 200 | No |
| Rider NEM-A Aggregated Net Energy Metering | Yes | 1000 | No |
| Rider NBT-L Large Customer Net Billing Tariff | Yes | 4000 | No |

## Points of the table

- The legacy rider shows a storage limit of 0 kWh because storage is not allowed under it.
- Under the five riders that allow storage, the paired battery capacity may equal the figure in the table; a larger battery is outside the rider's limit.
- No rider allows energy charged into the battery from the grid to be exported for credit.
- Hypothetical illustration: a 40 kWh battery is within the limit of Rider NEM-R and Rider NBT-R; a 45 kWh battery is within the limit of Rider NBT-C but not of the two residential riders.
